title: Fixture Scope
statement: Implement `solve(scope)`. `scope` is `function` or `module`. Two tests append 1. Function scope gives the second test a fresh list, so it sees `[1]`. Module scope shares the list, so the second test sees `[1, 1]`. Return the second test's list. Any other scope returns `error`.
constraints: module leaks if the fixture is a list

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: A module-scoped mutable fixture is one object for every test in the module.

editorial: A module-scoped mutable fixture is one object for every test in the module. Appends accumulate. Function scope builds it again. The second test's list is the observation. Wider scope is a performance choice you only want for immutable fixtures.
